findings.evidence:
`pkg/privilege/privileges/privileges.go:387` calls `p.Handle.ensureActiveUser(user)` in `MatchIdentity` for every auth attempt, where `user` is client-supplied.
`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1899` `ensureActiveUser` loads data when `activeUsers` misses, then `merge` stores every username returned by `loadSomeUsers` into `activeUsers` (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1915`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1923`).
`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:448` `loadSomeUsers` always seeds `extendedUserList` with the input usernames and regenerates `userList` from that map (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:457`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:463`), so even a non-existent username becomes “active”. It also unconditionally loads the full `mysql.role_edges` table first (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:449`).
`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1934` `UpdateAll` periodically reloads privileges for *all* `activeUsers` (collected via `Range`) and again calls `loadSomeUsers`.
`pkg/domain/domain.go:1892` runs `do.privHandle.UpdateAll()` on the periodic timer, amplifying the effect over time.
findings.fix:
Avoid letting untrusted/unknown usernames permanently expand `activeUsers` and the refresh set. Options (minimal → stronger):
- Only add usernames to `activeUsers` after a successful identity match (i.e., after `matchIdentity` finds a record), not before.
- Or maintain a separate bounded/TTL negative-cache for non-existent usernames; keep `activeUsers` strictly “exists-in-mysql.user”.
- Defer loading full `mysql.role_edges` until after the user is known to exist / after authentication, or cache roleGraph separately with controlled refresh.
findings.impact: Availability/security: an unauthenticated client can attempt many distinct usernames to (1) force repeated full scans/loads of `mysql.role_edges` and multiple privilege-table queries per new username, and (2) grow `activeUsers` without bound. This can inflate periodic privilege refresh work (`UpdateAll`), generate very large SQL predicates (many `OR USER = ...`), increase memory usage, and in extreme cases cause privilege refresh failures, severe CPU/IO load, or OOM.
findings.verify: Stress scenario: open many connections with unique random usernames (no password needed to hit `MatchIdentity`), and observe CPU/latency/memory over time and during the periodic privilege refresh loop. Confirm that `activeUsers` does not grow unbounded and that refresh work remains bounded (and does not repeatedly full-scan `mysql.role_edges` per unknown username).
findings.what: Potential unauthenticated DoS/perf regression: `MatchIdentity` calls `ensureActiveUser` on client-supplied usernames, and `ensureActiveUser` unconditionally loads the full role graph and records the (even non-existent) username into `activeUsers`. Over time, `activeUsers` can grow without bound, and periodic privilege refresh (`UpdateAll`) reloads based on this expanding set, amplifying CPU/IO/memory usage.

subject: *: avoid notify privilege update for all users (#57042)
summary: Reviewed commit vs parent focusing on executor/privilege/session changes around per-user privilege reload notifications. Found a High-severity availability risk: client-supplied usernames can permanently expand the active-user privilege cache and trigger repeated full role-graph loads, enabling unauthenticated DoS/perf degradation; this behavior is still present up to upstream/master.
